title: Start with the decision. Then build the dashboard.
description: A practical way to turn a reporting request into a clear business question, a useful measure and a dashboard someone can act on.
author: Karol Songin
takeaway: A useful dashboard connects a number to a decision, an owner and a next step.

sources.label: Microsoft: dashboard design tips in Power BI

sections.heading: What decision should the report help you make?
sections.body: Imagine a team reviewing its open customer enquiries. A total enquiry count shows how much work exists, but it does not tell the team which customer needs a response today. Start by asking what someone should do differently after reading the report.
bullets: Name the person who will use the information.
Write down the decision they need to make.
Agree how often the information needs to change.

callout.title: A question worth answering
callout.body: Which enquiries have been waiting more than two working days, and who is responsible for the next response?

sections.heading: Turn a broad request into a useful measure
sections.body: A request such as ‘show our enquiries’ needs a little more definition before anyone builds a visual. Agree what counts, how dates are handled and what action follows. The same approach works for orders, outstanding invoices or delayed jobs.

rows: Which customers need a response today?
Open enquiries without a response for two working days
The person assigned to the enquiry
Review the enquiry and contact the customer

sections.heading: Check the numbers before you trust the chart
sections.body: Pick a small set of records from the source system and trace them through the calculation. Check an enquiry opened before a weekend, one that has already been answered and one without an assigned owner. Write down the expected result before checking the dashboard.

callout.title: Keep the check repeatable
callout.body: A clear definition and a few agreed test records make future changes easier to verify.

sections.heading: Give the reader a clear next step
sections.body: Keep the important decision visible. Put enquiries needing attention next to their owner and last response date. Let the reader move from a summary to the underlying records, so they can investigate and act without hunting through another spreadsheet.

seoTitle: Planning a Business Dashboard: Questions to Ask
